author: Wolfgang Herfort and Luis Ribes
title: Torsion elements and centralizers in free products of profinite groups
publication: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik358 (1985),155–161
status: Full original obtained; all seven original pages visually read
pdf_page_rule: PDF page1 is archive cover; original printed page = PDF page+153 for PDF pages2–8.

theorem_anchors.evidence: Every finite-order element of a finite free pro-C product is conjugate into a factor. Complete proof read: finite-factor reduction; Kurosh decomposition for open subgroup generated by x and an open normal subgroup; Cartesian-kernel order calculation; prime-power and distinct-prime cases via wreath-product separation.
A_i intersect A_i^g is trivial for g outside A_i; centralizer of a nontrivial factor element equals its centralizer in that factor. Full proof read through Lemma3 and finite-factor reduction.
Every finite subgroup of a free product of two pro-C groups is conjugate into a factor; proof uses TheoremA′ and Lemma3(ii).

Generalization to compact indexed free pro-C products, including finite-subgroup conjugacy in(i), torsion in(ii), malnormality in(iii), centralizers in(iv). This supports the finite two-factor application but is more general than required.

application: D.27: an actual continuous automorphism of C2 coproduct C3 sends the two torsion generators to conjugates of the appropriate factors. This necessity result does not turn an obstructed selected finite certificate into an exclusion of every homology correction in its CM matrix coset.
